name: – Billy Kelleher – After § 19 – Am 7
title: REPORT on gender inequalities in health, specifically as regards gender-specific conditions
part_text: 19a. Recalls that the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion is guaranteed by Article 10 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and that the right to conscientious objection is recognised in accordance with the national laws governing its exercise; stresses that healthcare professionals should not be compelled to perform specific medical acts to which they have a sincere objection on grounds of conscience, provided that this right is exercised in accordance with applicable national law, professional and ethical standards and the duty to provide emergency care, and provided that patients are informed in a timely manner and that continuity of care is ensured;
